chapter_theme: The ancient way of initiation (சம்பிரதாயம்): the guru takes the disciple's body, wealth and life with water, places hand and feet on him, cuts the clinging of deeds and births, and shows the Lord within; the disciple, exchanged for the guru himself, comes to know no difference between I and you, Siva and soul, as body and life are one.
structure_note: The rite and its effects (1778 to 1785), in which the giving of body, wealth and life recurs (1778, 1783, 1784); then the fruit of it, awareness and grace (1786, 1787), and the non-difference of the soul and the Lord (1788 to 1791).

1778.reading: Taking body, wealth and life with water, looking so that the clinging of spreading deeds is cut, placing his hand, setting his feet in an instant and making the awareness subtle, Nandi showed the way that cuts off birth.
1778.nuance: உதகத்தால் கொண்டு (taking with water) is the gesture of a gift sealed by pouring water; the disciple's body, wealth and life (tanu, artha, prana) are given over to the guru. The look, the hand and the feet are traditionally the initiations by sight, touch and the feet.

1779.reading: Life and body as the bright possession, the wondrous Supreme, the breath that follows after, Siva who acts and Chit-Shakti: the supreme guru took me, unable to save myself, so that I might be saved for the First One.
1779.nuance: The list in the first three lines is hard to construe; it may name what the guru took over or the levels through which he raised the disciple. உயலார் (those who cannot save themselves) is read as the disciple.

1780.reading: The thing the teacher set in the western direction and told me to think on every day lies below the crown and above the uvula; this is the state he set, with the mouth not opened.
1780.nuance: பச்சிம திக்கு (the western direction) is taken as the back of the head or the hidden rear path of the breath. The place between crown and palate and the closed mouth point to a yogic practice, but the verse does not spell it out.

1781.reading: Me, who wandered babbling everywhere, he swept clean, drew out all the dirt that sat within, and exchanged himself and me as on a balance: the rate matched and the trade turned out well.
1781.nuance: The image is a merchant's: தட்டொக்க (the scale pans level), வட்டம் (the rate or commission in an exchange), வாணிபம் (trade). The guru takes the disciple and gives himself. பிட்டடித்து is obscure; it may mean beating about, or be corrupt.

1782.reading: People do not know at all how the Lord of all the many lives that are borne abides; cutting through the strife of the dividing bindu, I have found the Lord who holds everything as in a womb.
1782.nuance: பிரிக்கின்ற விந்து (the bindu that divides) is taken as maya, which sets things apart; பிணக்கு is the conflict or tangle it makes. கருக்கொண்ட may mean holding all as a womb holds, or holding the seed of all.

1783.reading: Taking note of the body, wealth and life that come together, seeking and setting his feet, with the power of grace and jnana he removed all clinging to the body of suffering, and became one with what he had joined, having plunged into it.
1783.nuance: This repeats the rite of 1778. பாடல் உடல் is read as பாடு (suffering) with the body; குளிக்கொண்டே (having plunged, or having immersed) is obscure, perhaps the disciple immersed in the Lord.

1784.reading: He took my servitude as his own, he took my throng of life, wealth and body, and since he who gave all fruit has taken them, there is nothing I can say he took.
1784.nuance: கொண்டான் (he took) opens every line. The turn is that what he took was his own gift, so it cannot be counted as taken; the disciple's surrender gives nothing the guru did not already hold.

1785.reading: Those who do not come to know the truth of how the body and the one in the body join, the breath that guides, the soul that stays firm, and what holds the body that is taken away, are like ghosts.
1785.nuance: தேகம் and தேகி (body and the embodied one) are a pair; பறிக்கின்ற காயம் may be the body that is snatched away at death. The comparison with ghosts is that they have form without understanding.

1786.reading: To those with awareness the world appears as it is; those with awareness have no suffering that befalls them; the time when those with awareness came to know, those with awareness knew it and saw.
1786.nuance: உணர்வுடையார் (those who have awareness) opens every line. The last two lines are circular as written and their point is unclear; perhaps that the moment of knowing is known only by the knower.

1787.reading: What can I say to Nandi, who gave pure grace to those who wandered in the expanse of the body, spread out and then contracted in turiya and in the sakala state, and roamed through the thirty-six?
1787.nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the thirty-six tattvas; துரியம் and சகலம் are states of the soul (the fourth state, and the state of full embodiment). The movement described is the soul's wandering through the states and the tattvas before grace.

1788.reading: Nearing him, there is no difference such as I and you, standing together as flesh and the life in the flesh; as the gods abide in heaven, humans revel in bliss as in honey.
1788.nuance: The image of body and life (ஊன், ஊனுயிர்) for the union recurs in 1790 and 1791. The verse claims non-difference while keeping the image of two that live together.

1789.reading: He and he do not know him; if one knows him, there is no knower left; if he and he know him, he and he become this one.
1789.nuance: A riddle built on அவன் (he) and இவன் (this one). It is traditionally read as the soul and the bond (or the soul and its awareness) that do not know the Lord, and the knower lost in knowing him; the referents are not fixed by the verse.

1790.reading: He who stood saying 'I am this' every day is there as the awareness within, as life in this flesh; he is there pouring like the great cloud of the sky; and I become the Lord of the space as well.
1790.nuance: நான் இது தான் is unclear: the Lord identifying with the soul, or the soul with the Lord. அம்பர நாதன் may be the Lord of the sky or of the hall (அம்பலம்); the last line claims the speaker becomes him.

1791.reading: The great Lord's nature and mine were never separate as 'he' and 'I', and the Lord knows it; Uma is truly joined as body and life, and the lord of the gods makes it right beforehand.
1791.nuance: The last two lines are unclear: உமை மெய்யே may mean Uma is the body (மெய்) while Siva is life, or 'Uma, truly'. திருந்த முன் செய்கின்ற may be the Lord preparing the soul beforehand.

links.note: Both describe the same rite: taking body, wealth and life, setting the feet and cutting the clinging; 1783 adds the power of grace and jnana and the guru becoming one with the disciple.
In 1594 the guru takes hold of the soul's three forms and takes the disciple to save him; 1784 makes the same taking of life, wealth and body, and adds that what he took was his own gift.
Both make the guru's hand on the disciple the moment of release: in 1590 the red guru places his hand on the head; in 1778 he places hand and feet and shows the way out of birth.
Both call a failure of understanding ghostly: the Kural's man who denies what the world holds to be is counted a demon, Tirumular's who don't know how body, breath and soul join are like ghosts.
Both make true knowing the end of suffering: the Kural's one who knows the support and lives so that clinging ends is not touched by the pains, Tirumular's who have awareness have no suffering.
Both describe the union by the image of flesh, or body, and the life within it, and both deny any 'I' and 'you' apart.

source_issues: 1781: பிட்டடித்து in line 1 is obscure and may be corrupt.
1783: பாடல் in line 3 and குளிக்கொண்டே in line 4 are obscure.
1786: lines 3 and 4 are circular as written; a word may be corrupt.
